purpose: OpenSPM content patches (docs/CONTENT-API.md): exact, checked single-instruction recipes applied to the player's own main.dol image, never shipped game code. Every patch must leave vanilla behaviour unchanged when no mod content is registered (it may only grow a buffer, widen a range the game never reaches on its own, or similar). The build applies them to the player-local codegen DOL before recompiling; the backend applies them to the boot image in guest RAM. include/openspm/code_patches.h mirrors this list (generated by tools/native_bridge/openspm_code_patches.py --write-header; test_code_patches.py keeps them equal). "relocations" are tables the backend copies at boot to their new home before the game runs.

patches.name: chartab-list-alloc
patches.why: Pause menu character tab (0x80195698) allocates its list for 5 entries of 12 bytes (li r4, 60); grow it to 64 entries (768 bytes, only while the menu is open) so OpenSPM can list registered characters. The game still fills at most 4 and its shared list code (0x80197B30) scrolls any count 8 rows at a time.

patches.name: chartab-list-clear
patches.why: The memset that clears that list (li r5, 60) covers the grown size.

patches.name: pixltab-list-alloc
patches.why: Pause menu Pixl tab (0x80196070) allocates its list for 17 entries (li r4, 204); grow it to 64 so OpenSPM can list added Pixls. The game still fills at most 16.

patches.name: pixltab-list-clear
patches.why: The memset that clears that list (li r5, 204) covers the grown size.

patches.name: char-id-properties-switch
patches.why: marioApplyCharacterProperties switches on the id for the hitbox size; ids above its bound (cmpwi r5, 4) skip it. Bound 127: an added character takes Mario's branch.

patches.name: char-id-change-files
patches.why: Move 71 (the switch transition) indexes its file table by the change target (rlwinm r30, r0, 3, 0, 28); the mask keeps the low two bits (rlwinm r30, r0, 3, 27, 28): Mario's files for an added character.

patches.name: char-id-screen-box
patches.why: 0x801532DC (a character's screen box, for the flip) takes the id as its first argument; its copy mr r24, r3 becomes rlwinm r24, r3, 0, 30, 31, which covers every caller.

patches.name: char-id-request-assert
patches.why: The character change request (0x80146DB0) asserts 0 <= id < 4; the bound becomes 128.

patches.name: char-id-request-assert-2
patches.why: The same assert in the second change request (0x80146ED4).

patches.name: map-registry-bound-0
patches.why: mapDataPtr's count check: 468 game maps + 64 spare slots.

patches.name: map-registry-bound-1
patches.why: mapDataPtr's name loop: 468 game maps + 64 spare slots.

patches.name: map-registry-bound-2
patches.why: mapDataEvtPtr's count check: 468 game maps + 64 spare slots.

patches.name: map-registry-bound-3
patches.why: mapDataEvtPtr's name loop: 468 game maps + 64 spare slots.

patches.name: enemy-template-bound
patches.why: npcdrv.c asserts a template number < 435 (NPCTEMPLATE_MAX); 435 + 64 spare rows.

relocations.name: item-data
relocations.why: itemDataTable (538 entries x 0x2C). All 86 code references (lis 0x803B + addi 0x7E78; the lis register serves nothing else and no data points into the table) are the item-data-NN patches above, which move the table to MEM2 above the game's arena where OpenSPM appends added items (ids 538+). The original stays in place, untouched. In relF (loaded at runtime at a layout the build derives from the player's files) the build finds the table's references itself with tools/content/table_refs.py and requires exactly relf_references clean ones; the game's REL loader writes relF at runtime, so those live in the recompiled module only.

relocations.name: char-model
relocations.why: A per-character table a mod fills (docs/CHARACTER-IDS.md): the game's 4 rows are copied and the other rows start as row 0 (Mario) until the roster writes an added character's. Code that reaches the table through a base register shared with neighbouring data keeps the original (its id reads are masked to 0-3).

relocations.name: map-registry
relocations.why: The map registry (docs/CUSTOM-LEVELS.md): the game's 468 map pointers, then spare slots that start as a copy of slot 0 (the count check needs every slot non-NULL; a lookup finds the game's own record first) until OpenSPM registers a map in one.

relocations.name: enemy-tribes
relocations.why: Enemy tables (docs/CUSTOM-LEVELS.md): the game's 535 rows, then 64 spare rows that start as a copy of row 0 until OpenSPM registers an enemy in one. Data words naming particular game rows keep reading the unchanged MEM1 copy.
